title: Majestic Deception
summary: Refuse the tempting queen promotion: a checking bishop sacrifice sets up a knight promotion with mate.

nodes.question: What must White do about ...Qg7 mate?
nodes.explanation: Begin after ...Nxe8. The rook has already been sacrificed; promoting a queen immediately ignores Black’s mating threat.

branches.title: Offer the bishop, then promote with mate
commentary: This seven-piece diagram begins after the earlier eight-piece rook interference sequence. That earlier sequence remains source context.
Bg5+ gives a forcing check and offers the bishop. White must use the reply to decide which promotion is safe.
Kxf7 removes the f-pawn and keeps control of g7, preserving the threat of ...Qg7 mate.
d8=N# promotes with check. The knight attacks f7, the bishop covers e7 and f6, Kh7 covers g6/g7/g8, and Black’s own queen and knight occupy f8/e8.
branches.explanation: d8=N# promotes with check. The knight attacks f7, the bishop covers e7 and f6, Kh7 covers g6/g7/g8, and Black’s own queen and knight occupy f8/e8.

branches.title: Capture the offered bishop
commentary: Compare Black’s capture of the checking bishop rather than the pawn.
Bg5+ offers material with check, forcing the king to choose between captures or a retreat.
Kxg5 accepts the bishop but abandons the king’s support of g7. Black can no longer deliver the same protected queen mate.
fxe8=Q captures the knight with the f-pawn, keeping the d7 pawn alive. The exact resulting queen ending is winning; choosing the d-pawn for this capture instead would draw.
branches.explanation: fxe8=Q captures the knight with the f-pawn, keeping the d7 pawn alive. The exact resulting queen ending is winning; choosing the d-pawn for this capture instead would draw.

branches.title: Promote before addressing the threat
commentary: Test the natural capture-promotion immediately after ...Nxe8.
dxe8=Q gains a queen but gives Black a forced mate. White’s material gain does not address king safety.
Qg7# is protected by Kf6. White’s Kh7 cannot capture the queen, and its queen and bishop cannot interpose against adjacent check.
branches.explanation: Qg7# is protected by Kf6. White’s Kh7 cannot capture the queen, and its queen and bishop cannot interpose against adjacent check.

branches.title: Choose a queen after ...Kxf7
commentary: Even after the bishop check, the promotion choice matters.
Bg5+ forces Black to respond to check.
Kxf7 keeps g7 protected while removing the other passer.
d8=Q loses because it fails to check the king on f7. The knight promotion would have ended the game immediately.
Qg7# punishes the lost tempo. The black king protects the queen and White has no legal defense.
branches.explanation: Qg7# punishes the lost tempo. The black king protects the queen and White has no legal defense.

branches.title: Use the wrong pawn to capture the knight
commentary: Compare the two pawns that can capture e8 after the bishop is taken.
Bg5+ forces the king to answer check while offering the bishop.
Kxg5 removes the bishop and leaves both white pawns able to capture Ne8.
dxe8=Q preserves f7 rather than d7. This exact queen-and-pawn ending is drawn with best play; fxe8=Q is the winning capture.
branches.classification: independent comparison of the two legal capture-promotions
branches.explanation: dxe8=Q preserves f7 rather than d7. This exact queen-and-pawn ending is drawn with best play; fxe8=Q is the winning capture.

exercises.prompt: Why is the knight stronger than a queen after ...Kxf7?
exercises.answer: Only the knight promotion checks f7. With the bishop and king controlling the remaining flights, that check is mate; a queen promotion permits ...Qg7#.

startContext: Begin after ...Nxe8 at 82 seconds, the visually reconstructed seven-piece position. The earlier d7, ...Qf8 and Re8 sacrifice belong to an eight-piece setup and remain unverified source context here. Selected later alternatives are checked exactly.
verification_scope: Saved board images reviewed manually. Every encoded intermediate position and endpoint is checked against the tablebase. Selected instructive variations, not an exhaustive tree of all legal defenses.
sourceCorrections: Capture-promotion is made explicit from the visual sequence: after ...Kxg5, fxe8=Q wins and preserves d7; the independently tested dxe8=Q comparison draws.
